title: Blackfoot musician and Native students at Gonzaga
summary: At Gonzaga he befriended a brilliant Blackfoot tenor saxophonist and other Native students.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Then I met this Indian, Blackfoot Indian out at Gonzaga University when I was studying pre-law. He was a musician, a real one. He was a genius. He came from a reservation, and nobody knows where he learned everything. But he played tenor saxophone, and he wrote arrangements without scores, and he had perfect pitch. He didn't a piano, it didn't mean anything to him. It was there in his head. And he heard me playing; I was trying to play like Freddie Kreitzer with Lombardo. I was in the gymnasium one day, playing. He came wandering in there -- I didn't know him...

He'd come over there on a scholarship. They had brought about six Indians over there -- some Sioux, Blackfoot, Nez Perce(?)... And they were my best friends! I liked them better than I liked anybody in the whole school.
